newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's ruling party receives new ETA death threat.
newsitem.headline: Spain's ruling party receives new ETA death threat.

text.p: The Basque guerrilla group ETA has threatened another Basque town councillor from Spain's ruling party, just days after it kidnapped and killed a young politician and sparked massive nationwide street protests.

"It's true that a new threat against a member of the PP (Popular Party) has appeared. We will reinforce all security measures," Angel Acebes, general coordinator of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's party, told reporters on Tuesday.
Acebes said he could confirm newspaper reports that another Basque town councillor had received a death threat on Monday.

The daily El Pais said Jose Luis Caso, 63, the only Popular Party official in the town of Renteria near San Sebastian, was the target. ETA graffiti appeared on town walls saying "You will be the next one", the paper said.
Caso said he did not want to make a big issue out of the graffiti.

"I don't want to worry about it too much because I know that defending certain ideas in the Basque country carries a risk. Whatever they say to me, I'm going to continue thinking the same," he told El Pais.
Separatist guerrillas kidnapped Miguel Angel Blanco, a 29-year-old councillor, in the Basque town of Ermua last Thursday and shot him twice in the head on Saturday. He died early the next day.
Acebes said he knew members of the Popular Party were a chief ETA target, but their threats would not make the conservative ruling party change its policies.

"For all the threats they make, for all the harm they try to cause, they are not going to make us renounce our objectives, our ideals of a Spain of peace, freedom, democracy, presided over by the rule of law," he said.
ETA, which has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968, has attacked Popular Party members in the past.
Aznar himself only barely escaped with his life when ETA set a car bomb off in April 1995.
